title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily — 2026-10-23
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-recent-paper ordering, not a popularity ranking. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old, and Semantic Scholar citation counts were unavailable in the retrieved snapshot and were not used.

sections.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
sections.abstract: The authors introduce MCP-Injector, a calibrated fault-injection middleware, and report that realistic MCP faults sharply reduce task performance while the tested larger gpt-oss model does not show better fault tolerance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present protocol-aware MCP fault injection calibrated to public ecosystem incidents and use it to test three agent stacks and two model sizes.
sections.unique_caveat: The scale comparison covers two gpt-oss sizes, 25 tasks, and three seeds under a permanent-heavy stress profile; the authors identify multi-server orchestration and longer-horizon tasks as open extensions.

sections.title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
sections.abstract: SWE-Shift compares matched clean and shifted continuations to test whether coding agents can preserve valid work and recover when task-relevant workspace changes occur mid-execution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce matched Clean/Shifted continuations and report lower shifted success for all 17 tested systems, with failures in state recovery, work preservation, and evidence freshness.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note 120 designed scenarios (some share task roots), one update per run, uncontrolled model randomness, a fixed post-fork token budget, and diagnostic controls covering five systems.

sections.title: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
sections.abstract: POSEIDON mines scientific repositories into executable, verifiable agent-training tasks; the authors report a 97,659-environment collection from 7,110 repositories and gains for fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models on six scientific-agent benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive Reproduction, Subflow, Completion, and Correction tasks from scientific workflows and add recursive verification/refinement; on a matched repository budget they report 9.3 times as many environments as the comparison pipeline.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported fine-tuning experiments use three Qwen3.5 variants and six selected benchmarks; the authors' independent manual quality audit sampled 600 tasks rather than the full corpus.

sections.title: SCI-AGENT-EXAM: Benchmarking Agents on Scientific Research Tasks
sections.abstract: SCI-AGENT-EXAM evaluates scientific agents on 120 expert-curated tasks across 11 fields and seven research task types, scoring executable and textual artifacts with a hybrid protocol.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine deterministic checks for executable outputs with a calibrated, expert-validated LLM judge for text, and analyze solution progress and stability as well as final outcomes.
sections.unique_caveat: Findings are bounded to 120 curated tasks and the 10 evaluated agents; textual-output scoring partly depends on an LLM judge, even though the authors report calibration and expert validation.

sections.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
sections.abstract: The authors propose measures for evaluating model–harness interactions and report that harness rankings vary across models and benchmarks, with valid completion and task correctness sometimes favoring different pairings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define five interaction-aware measures, including Valid Completion Rate and Model-Harness Fit, to separate task outcome from execution reliability and token load.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparisons cover four general-purpose harnesses, four core models, and six benchmarks; the paper itself finds rankings vary with the selected model and benchmark, so no single harness ordering generalizes automatically.

sections.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
sections.abstract: RobustRLlib unifies 17 robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms and evaluates them over 273 perturbation configurations, mapping where tested methods retain robustness and where gaps remain.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a shared interface for 17 algorithms plus an extensible shift-oriented evaluation platform and capability map.
sections.unique_caveat: The capability map is limited to the included algorithms, tasks, and 273 declared perturbation configurations; it cannot establish robustness to untested deployment shifts.

sections.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors use topic prompts to generate synthetic questions and privileged reasoning traces for on-policy self-training, reporting gains on language benchmarks and visual question answering without human-curated task prompts or answers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a curriculum-generation and privileged-demonstration process driven by coarse topic descriptions alone.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports standard language benchmarks and VQA, but does not establish generality beyond the evaluated tasks or that self-generated supervision is reliable in open-ended deployment.

sections.title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
sections.abstract: TopKLoRA activates only the largest adapter latents per token; in sleeper-agent backdoor experiments, the authors report identifying and ablating circuits necessary and sufficient for the backdoor while preserving instruction-following performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors extend TopKLoRA as an interpretable-by-design adapter and use sparse latents to search for circuits, then test the identified circuits by ablation and gradient routing.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is a sleeper-agent backdoor case study using Gemma 2 2B and Qwen2.5 1.5B/7B; broader backdoor families and larger model scales are not established by this experiment.

sections.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
sections.abstract: The authors use sparse-autoencoder features from OpenVLA activations to predict task failure before an unrecoverable state and interpret recurring success- and failure-associated behavior patterns.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify outcome-predictive SAE features and use a VLM pipeline to produce behavior descriptions, then check their correspondence with activations on held-out intervals.
sections.unique_caveat: The study concerns OpenVLA activations and the authors describe the workshop version as non-archival; transfer to other VLA models, robots, and environments remains unshown here.

sections.title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: ActionRAG combines cautious entity indexing with query-time graph diffusion to refine evidence in long-term agent memory, reporting 55.1 average accuracy on MemoryAgentBench and a 5.4-point gain over its strongest retrieval-based baseline.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use tiered entity resolution, dual-channel retrieval, and query-conditioned graph diffusion to revise triple scores while protecting seed evidence.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is reported on MemoryAgentBench; latency is measured on consumer Apple Silicon, and the reported p99 figure sums separately measured retrieval-side components rather than an end-to-end cross-hardware benchmark.
